$why: Two roles, one per story kind: a test that proves an ALREADY-committed change, or a test that reproduces a bug a fix has already addressed. One body each -- the two say different things about whether the code under test is expected to pass, and conflating them produces a test written against the wrong expectation.
2026-08-16: the PROOF REQUIREMENT and the DIFF HEADING moved here too.
Both were string literals in brownfield-repro-test-writer.sh, assigned to _req_proof and
_diff_heading and injected into this same prompt as __REQ_PROOF__ / __DIFF_HEADING__. So the
role sentence lived in the template while the sentence that actually decides whether the test is
acceptable — 'it must FAIL against the pre-fix code and PASS with the fix' — lived in a shell
script, where no prompt review reaches it and it could not be diffed against the role it pairs
with. They vary together on exactly the same condition (story kind), so they belong in the same
description: What kind of test the repro-writer is being asked for, by story kind.

bodies.proves_committed_change: write ONE test that proves a change which has ALREADY been implemented and committed
bodies.reproduces_fixed_bug: write ONE bug-reproducing test for a fix that has ALREADY been implemented and committed
bodies.proof_proves_committed_change: 3. The test MUST prove the verification criteria above against the committed change. Assert the observable outcome the change now produces — not the mechanism, and not that some prior behaviour was broken. This is a NEW capability: there is no pre-fix failure to reproduce, and a test written as though there were will be rejected. It MUST PASS with the change in place.
bodies.proof_reproduces_fixed_bug: 3. The test MUST genuinely REPRODUCE the bug: it must FAIL against the pre-fix code and PASS with the fix. Assert the corrected observable value — a test that passes regardless of the fix is worthless and will be rejected.
bodies.heading_proves_committed_change: The change that was just made (diff vs baseline)
bodies.heading_reproduces_fixed_bug: The fix that was just made (diff vs baseline)
